objects.description: ALSA-specific stream info structure for PortAudio. Used via PaStreamParameters::hostApiSpecificStreamInfo to pass ALSA options when opening a stream. Fields include the struct size, host API type identifier (should be paALSA), a version field, and an optional device string for selecting ALSA device by name. Exact accepted values for version and deviceString are not fully documented here.

functions.name: PaAlsa_InitializeStreamInfo
functions.description: Initializes an ALSA-specific stream info structure prior to setting any ALSA-specific attributes on it. Typical usage is to allocate a PaAlsaStreamInfo, call this initializer, then populate fields such as deviceString before passing it via PaStreamParameters::hostApiSpecificStreamInfo when opening a stream.
requirements: info must point to a writable PaAlsaStreamInfo instance.
Call this before writing any fields that will be used by PortAudio when opening a stream.

functions.name: PaAlsa_EnableRealtimeScheduling
functions.description: Configures whether the audio callback thread for the given stream should run with realtime (FIFO) scheduling when the stream is started. Set enable to nonzero to request realtime scheduling, or zero to disable. The setting affects thread creation at stream start.
requirements: s must be a valid PaStream pointer associated with the ALSA host API.
To affect the scheduling policy of the callback thread, call this before starting the stream (i.e., prior to Pa_StartStream on s).
enable is treated as a boolean flag; nonzero enables, zero disables. Other integer values have unspecified effect beyond boolean interpretation.

functions.name: PaAlsa_GetStreamInputCard
functions.description: Retrieves the ALSA card index backing the input device for the specified PortAudio stream. Useful when integrating with raw ALSA APIs or for diagnostics.
requirements: s must be a valid PaStream opened on the ALSA host API.
card must be a non-NULL pointer to an int where the card index will be written.
The call may fail if the stream does not have an input device or if the host API is not ALSA (error code depends on implementation).
Check the returned PaError; on success, *card is set to the ALSA card index.

functions.name: PaAlsa_GetStreamOutputCard
functions.description: Retrieves the ALSA card index backing the output device for the specified PortAudio stream. Useful for interop with ALSA or for logging.
requirements: s must be a valid PaStream opened on the ALSA host API.
card must be a non-NULL pointer to an int where the card index will be written.
The call may fail if the stream does not have an output device or if the host API is not ALSA (error code depends on implementation).
Always check the returned PaError; on success, *card receives the ALSA card index.

functions.name: PaAlsa_SetNumPeriods
functions.description: Sets the number of ALSA periods (buffer fragments) PortAudio will configure devices with. By default, 4 periods are used. Adjusting this can affect latency and stability. Typically called before opening ALSA streams so new streams use the specified period count.
requirements: numPeriods is an integer specifying the number of periods; exact valid range is unknown from this header.
Callers should check the returned PaError to confirm the setting was accepted.
The effect and applicability are ALSA-specific; non-ALSA hosts are not affected.

functions.name: PaAlsa_SetRetriesBusy
functions.description: Sets how many times PortAudio should retry opening a busy ALSA device, sleeping a short interval between attempts. Use to improve robustness when devices are temporarily busy.
requirements: retries is an integer count of retry attempts; valid range is not specified in this header.
Callers should check the returned PaError to ensure the setting was applied.
This setting applies to ALSA device opening; other host APIs are unaffected.

functions.name: PaAlsa_SetLibraryPathName
functions.description: Overrides the ALSA library filename/path PortAudio will use when compiled to load ALSA dynamically (PA_ALSA_DYNAMIC). If only a filename is provided, the dynamic loader will search standard library paths (e.g., /usr/lib, /usr/local/lib).
requirements: pathName must point to a NUL-terminated string naming the ALSA shared library (full path or filename).
Only meaningful when PortAudio is built with dynamic ALSA loading (PA_ALSA_DYNAMIC).
Should be called before any operation that triggers loading of the ALSA library.

data_types.description: A NUL-terminated string that represents a filesystem path or filename. May be absolute or relative. For shared libraries on Linux this often looks like libasound.so, libasound.so.2, or /usr/lib/libasound.so.
A NUL-terminated string naming an ALSA PCM device. Typical forms include hw:0,0, plughw:1, default, or more complex strings accepted by ALSA device parsing. Used to select the ALSA device by name.

generators.generator:
import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target: Provide interesting, valid filesystem path strings for ALSA shared libraries
# Used by fuzzer stub FUZZ_PARAM_STR feeding PaAlsa_SetLibraryPathName
# Must return bytes (NUL-terminated not required by wrapper, but C++ std::string provides implicit NUL).
# We generate ASCII/UTF-8 paths typical on Linux with variety of forms.

LIB_BASENAMES = [
    "libasound.so",
    "libasound.so.2",
    "libasound.so.2.0.0",
    "asound.so",
    "libasound",
]

PREFIX_DIRS = [
    "/usr/lib",
    "/usr/lib64",
    "/usr/local/lib",
    "/lib",
    "/lib64",
    "/opt/lib",
]

REL_PREFIXES = [
    ".",
    "..",
    "./lib",
    "../lib",
]

SUFFIXES = [
    "",
    ".2",
    ".2.0.0",
]

ALT_NAMES = [
    "libasound_module_conf_pulse.so",
    "libasound_module_pcm_pulse.so",
    "libasound_module_pcm_jack.so",
    "libasound_module_rate.so",
]

# Include some unusual but valid characters and spaces
SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "._-"
EXTRA_CHARS = " ()[]{}+,=@!#%"  # avoid path separators and NUL


def _rand_name(r: random.Random, min_len: int = 3, max_len: int = 12) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(r.choice(SAFE_CHARS + EXTRA_CHARS) for _ in range(n)).strip()


def _maybe_versioned(r: random.Random, base: str) -> str:
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        return base
    # Append 1-3 numeric dotted components
    parts = []
    for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3)):
        parts.append(str(r.randint(0, 10)))
    return base + "." + ".".join(parts)


def _with_env_var(r: random.Random, path: str) -> str:
    # Embed common Linux env vars occasionally
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        var = r.choice(["LD_LIBRARY_PATH", "HOME", "PWD", "OLDPWD"])
        prefix = "${" + var + "}"
        # Prepend or replace dirname
        if path.startswith("/"):
            # Replace root with env prefix
            rest = path.lstrip("/")
            return prefix + "/" + rest
        else:
            return prefix + "/" + path
    return path


def _make_absolute(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Absolute paths with common directories and optional subdirs
    base_dir = r.choice(PREFIX_DIRS)
    # Optionally add architecture triplet subdir
    subdirs: List[str] = []
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        subdirs.append(r.choice([
            "x86_64-linux-gnu",
            "aarch64-linux-gnu",
            "arm-linux-gnueabihf",
            "i386-linux-gnu",
        ]))
    # Optional "alsa" or "pulseaudio" subdir, though uncommon for lib
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        subdirs.append(r.choice(["alsa", "pulseaudio"]))
    # Choose a library name
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        lib = r.choice(LIB_BASENAMES)
    else:
        lib = r.choice(ALT_NAMES)
    # Optionally add extra version suffix (can duplicate but remains plausible)
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        lib = _maybe_versioned(r, lib)
    path = "/".join([base_dir] + subdirs + [lib])
    # Occasionally add a trailing space or uncommon but valid characters
    if r.random() < 0.15:
        path += r.choice([" ", "\t"])  # spaces in filenames are valid
    return path


def _make_relative(r: random.Random) -> str:
    prefix = r.choice(REL_PREFIXES)
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        name = r.choice(LIB_BASENAMES)
    else:
        # Construct a plausible lib name
        comp = _rand_name(r)
        if not comp.startswith("lib"):
            comp = "lib" + comp
        if not comp.endswith(".so"):
            comp += ".so"
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            comp = _maybe_versioned(r, comp)
        name = comp
    # Optionally include subdirectories
    parts = [prefix]
    for _ in range(r.randint(0, 2)):
        parts.append(_rand_name(r))
    parts.append(name)
    return "/".join(parts)


def _make_basename(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Just the library filename, to rely on system search path
    if r.random() < 0.8:
        name = r.choice(LIB_BASENAMES)
    else:
        name = r.choice(ALT_NAMES)
    # Optionally add additional numeric version suffix
    if r.random() < 0.25:
        name = _maybe_versioned(r, name)
    return name


def _add_prefixes(r: random.Random, path: str) -> str:
    # Prepend ./ or ../ occasionally even for absolute-like names (not for real absolutes)
    if not path.startswith("/") and r.random() < 0.3:
        path = r.choice(["./", "../"]) + path
    # Environment variable expansion chance
    path = _with_env_var(r, path)
    return path


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose one of several path styles
    style = r.random()
    if style < 0.45:
        candidate = _make_basename(r)
    elif style < 0.8:
        candidate = _make_absolute(r)
    else:
        candidate = _make_relative(r)

    candidate = _add_prefixes(r, candidate)

    # Limit size to 4096 bytes as per constraint
    s = candidate[:4096]
    # Ensure non-empty; fallback to a valid common name
    if not s:
        s = "libasound.so"

    # Return UTF-8 bytes; C++ stub will use std::string and ensure NUL-termination internally.
    return s.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
